## 任务：撰写论文 Experiments 章节 (§4)

### 写作前必读
1. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md` — LaTeX 写作规范
2. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/red-section.skill.md` — 写作红线

### 论文背景
**标题**: "When Does Non-Uniform KV Cache Quantization Help? Cardinality Constraints and a Heterogeneity Diagnostic"
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR), 8 pages
**Core claim**: 一个 cardinality constraint (max_2bit≤k) 修复 hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16} 上的 per-head KV cache quantization 失败。收益与 head sensitivity heterogeneity 正相关。

### 章节结构与 Word Budget
~1200 words total. 5 subsections:

### §4.1 Experimental Setup (~250 words)

**模型**:
- Qwen2.5-7B: GQA ratio 7:1, 28 layers × 4 KV heads = 112 KV heads
- Llama-3.1-8B: GQA ratio 4:1, 32 layers × 8 KV heads = 256 KV heads
- Mistral-7B-v0.3: GQA ratio 4:1, 32 layers × 8 KV heads = 256 KV heads, sliding window attention

**评估**:
- Dataset: WikiText-2 test split (298,938 tokens)
- Metric: perplexity (PPL, ↓ better), bf16 inference, stride=512
- 下游任务: ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande (0-shot)

**Profiling**:
- Per-head PPL-based distortion: quantize each head independently to each bit-width, measure PPL increase
- Hires calibration: 64 sequences × 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train
- Action space: {2, 4, 8, 16}-bit per head

**Compression**:
- Default: 4× compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio=0.25)
- Constraint: max_2bit ≤ k, where k determined via compounding sweep (k=8 for Qwen 112 heads)
- For Llama/Mistral (256 heads): also use compounding sweep to select k

**Baselines**:
- Uniform 4-bit quantization (all heads at 4-bit)
- Unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style \cite{zuo2026ratequant})
- Unconstrained MCKP allocation
- L0-random heuristic: Layer-0 heads at 8-bit, k random non-L0 heads at 2-bit, rest at 4-bit (5 seeds, report mean±std and median)
- Naive positional heuristic: Layer-0 at 8-bit, deepest k heads at 2-bit, rest at 4-bit

### §4.2 Main Results (~300 words)
**Table 1** — Cross-architecture main results at 4× compression:

```
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{PPL ($\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\times$ compression. Unconstrained allocation fails catastrophically on \{2,4,8,16\}; our cardinality constraint restores performance. Best constrained result per model in \textbf{bold}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
\toprule
Model & Baseline & Uniform & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Unconstrained} & Ours \\
 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & Greedy & MCKP & (Constr.) \\
\midrule
Qwen2.5-7B & 9.81 & 15.45 & 32.45 & 36.92 & \textbf{10.91} \\
Llama-3.1-8B & 8.09 & 8.47 & --- & --- & \textbf{8.45} \\
Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.04 & 7.13 & --- & --- & 7.16 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

**关键叙述点**:
- Qwen: constrained MCKP achieves 29.3% PPL reduction over uniform (10.91 vs 15.45)
- 没有 constraint 时，greedy (32.45) 和 MCKP (36.92) 都比 uniform (15.45) 差 — catastrophic failure
- Llama: marginal 0.2% improvement (8.45 vs 8.47) — low heterogeneity limits optimization headroom
- Mistral: slightly worse than uniform (7.16 vs 7.13, +0.4%) — genuine negative result; profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads
- 参考 Figure 3 (\ref{fig:allocation}) 展示 Qwen 的 bit 分配对比
- **注意**：Llama/Mistral 的 unconstrained 结果标 "---" 因为 unconstrained 实验只在 Qwen 上做了

**Figure 3 引用**:
```
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_allocation_comparison.pdf}
\caption{Bit-width allocation comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Uniform assigns all heads to 4-bit. Our constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit and selectively assigns 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.}
\label{fig:allocation}
\end{figure}
```

### §4.3 Budget Sweep (~200 words)
**Table 3** — Compression ratio ablation on Qwen2.5-7B:

| Compression | Budget | Uniform PPL | Constrained MCKP PPL | Δ PPL |
|------------|--------|-------------|----------------------|-------|
| 2× | 0.50 | 10.10 | 10.66 | −0.56 |
| 4× | 0.25 | 15.45 | 11.23 | +4.21 |
| 8× | 0.125 | 14,759 | 907 | +13,852 |

**叙述**:
- At 2×: uniform 8-bit is near-lossless (+0.29 PPL vs bf16); per-head optimization has no headroom → constrained MCKP slightly worse due to unnecessary 2-bit assignments
- At 4×: sweet spot — 29.3% improvement. Significant gap between uniform 4-bit and optimized allocation.
- At 8×: both methods degrade catastrophically, but constrained MCKP preserves Layer-0 at 8-bit, preventing total collapse (907 vs 14,759). Neither is practical, but demonstrates the protection mechanism.
- 结论: constrained allocation provides meaningful improvement at moderate-to-aggressive compression (≥4×)

### §4.4 Heuristic Baselines (~200 words)

L0-random baseline comparison across 3 models. 用 median 做主对比，supplementary 报 mean±std。

| Model | MCKP | L0-random median | L0-random mean±std | Naive positional |
|-------|------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Qwen2.5-7B | 10.91 | 11.52 | 11.69±0.42 | 12.23 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 8.45 | 10.04 | 10.48±1.03 | — |
| Mistral-7B-v0.3 | 7.32 | 7.59 | 7.56±0.09 | — |

**叙述**:
- Profiling-guided allocation (MCKP) consistently outperforms random L0-based heuristics
- Qwen: MCKP beats L0-random median by 0.61 PPL, naive positional by 1.32 PPL
- Llama: larger gap (MCKP 8.45 vs L0-random median 10.04) — random 2-bit assignment particularly harmful on 256-head architectures
- Mistral: small gap (7.32 vs 7.59) — consistent with low heterogeneity narrative
- High variance of L0-random on Llama (std=1.03) suggests 2-bit assignment is position-sensitive on this architecture

### §4.5 Downstream Evaluation (~200 words)

Qwen2.5-7B, 4× compression, 0-shot evaluation:

| Task | Baseline (bf16) | Uniform 4-bit | MCKP (Ours) | Δ vs Uniform |
|------|-----------------|---------------|-------------|--------------|
| ARC-C | — | 0.482 | 0.514 | +3.2 pts |
| HellaSwag | — | 0.728 | 0.768 | +4.0 pts |
| PIQA | — | 0.766 | 0.779 | +1.3 pts |
| WinoGrande | — | 0.662 | 0.682 | +2.0 pts |
| Average | 0.695 | 0.660 | 0.686 | +2.6 pts |

Recovery rate: (0.686 − 0.660) / (0.695 − 0.660) = 72.8%

**叙述**:
- PPL improvement transfers to downstream tasks: +2.6 points average accuracy over uniform
- Recovery rate 72.8%: constrained MCKP recovers nearly three-quarters of the accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit quantization
- Largest gain on HellaSwag (+4.0 pts) where language modeling quality matters most
- Consistent improvement across all 4 tasks — not cherry-picked

### 写作规范（红线）
1. **每个数字必须来自上面提供的数据**，不要凭记忆写数字
2. **禁止**: "consistently outperforms", "significantly improves", "state-of-the-art" — 只有 3 个模型，不足以用这些强度词
3. **诚实呈现负向结果**: Mistral 是 genuine negative，必须如实描述（profiler 零信号导致 MCKP 无优势）
4. **精度统一**: PPL 保留两位小数（如 10.91），下游 accuracy 保留三位小数（如 0.514）
5. **引用格式**: 用 `\cite{bibtex_key}` 引用文献
6. **不要写 "To the best of our knowledge"、"Extensive experiments demonstrate"**
7. **C4 cross-dataset 结果暂缓**：不要在本章节提及 C4 cross-dataset 实验

### 可用引用 (bibtex_keys)
liu2024kivi, hooper2024kvquant, lin2024qserve, he2024zipcache, kang2024gear, duanmu2024skvq, zhang2023h2o, li2024snapkv, ge2024fastgen, xiao2024streamingllm, liu2024scissorhands, yang2024pyramidinfer, zuo2026ratequant, lei2026arkv, li2025kvmix, zhang2025mixkvq, kim2024squeezellm

### 输出
将完整的 LaTeX 代码写入：
`/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0509_2/projects/ratekv/docs/paper/experiments.tex`

文件应包含 `\section{Experiments}` 开头，不包含 preamble 或 `\begin{document}`。使用 `\input{experiments}` 方式被 main.tex 引入。

### 完成标志
experiments.tex 包含 §4.1-4.5 全部内容，所有表格和图引用完整，无占位符数字。

---
name: paper-plan
description: 论文规划——生成 writing_plan.yaml 作为下游 Worker 的共享合约（投稿目标、outline、可视化、表格、文献策略、写作顺序）。当 Director 说"写论文"/"准备投稿"/"论文计划"时使用。
scope: global
tags:
  - workflow
  - research
  - planning
  - academic
version: 2
roles:
- agent
- paper_agent
---

## 触发条件

- 用户/Director 说"论文规划"/"paper plan"/"投稿计划"/"目标 NeurIPS/ICML/..."
- 核心方法验证成功后，主动建议制定论文计划
- 用户要求调整已有论文计划（重新生成 writing_plan.yaml）

## 产出

**唯一产出**：`projects/{name}/writing_plan.yaml` —— 所有下游 Worker（章节写作、画图、文献搜索）的共享合约。

文件格式见下方 §writing_plan.yaml 格式。生成后通过 `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", content)` 写入项目根目录。

## 步骤

### Step 1: 收集现状

1. `read_project_file("ideas.md")` — DECIDED（已验证）和 ACTIVE（待做）分区
2. `read_registry()` — 所有实验及状态、baseline 指标、metrics
3. `read_roadmap()` — 研究方向、实验矩阵、决策日志
4. `read_project_file("literature_map.yaml")` — 已有文献库（如存在）
5. `ls templates/latex/` — 确认目标 venue 模板可用性

### Step 2: 分析论文可行性（纯推理）

投稿门槛 mirror 自 `experiment-matrix` skill：

**投稿门槛（按 Director 指定的目标 venue 对标）**
- A 类（NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR）：3 个核心 contribution、主结果 ≥ 3 benchmark（含 ≥ 1 OOD）、Baseline ≥ 5、≥ 3 seed + 显著性、完整 ablation、≥ 1 efficiency、≥ 3 qualitative case
- 具体门槛由 Director 在审批 writing_plan 时把关，你只按 Director 指定的 venue 标准规划

**时间紧张时的应对（禁止降级目标 venue）**：
- 升级并行度：多 Worker 同时铺代码/数据/图表
- 砍低优先级维度（P2: efficiency/qualitative 可后补），集中火力在 P0 硬门槛
- 向 Director 汇报，由 Director 决定申请云 GPU 扩容或调整实验优先级
- **禁止自行建议更换目标会议**——venue 决策是 Director + 用户的权限

### Step 3: 模板选择

1. 查本地 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
2. 缺失时 WebSearch 搜索官方最新模板，spawn Worker 下载到 `templates/latex/{venue}{year}/`
3. 仍找不到 → 复用最近版本（如 neurips2025），在 `meta.template_note` 标注原因
4. 在 `writing_plan.yaml` 的 `meta.template` 字段写入实际路径

### Step 4: 生成 writing_plan.yaml

按 §writing_plan.yaml 格式生成完整 YAML，包含：

- `meta`：venue/track/template/page_limit/deadline/core_claim/created_at
- `paper_outline`：各章节 word_budget + core_bullets + dependencies + 章节关联的 `tables`/`figures`/`registry_refs`/`citation_hints`
- `visualization_plan`：每张图的 fig_id/type/tool/data_source/placement
- `table_plan`：每张表的 table_id/caption/type/columns/data_source（§3.7 新增）
- `literature_strategy`：citation_budget + macro_context + micro_clusters
- `writing_order`：严格串行的章节写作顺序

**关键填写规则**：

- `visualization_plan.tool`：概念图（架构图/流程图）→ `paperbanana`；统计图（柱/线/热力）→ `matplotlib`
- `table_plan.type`：`comparison` / `ablation` / `statistics` / `configuration`
- `table_plan.data_source`：能从 registry 提取的写 `"registry: exp_xxx, exp_yyy"`；不能的写 `"manual"`
- `paper_outline.{section}.tables` / `.figures`：把 `table_plan` / `visualization_plan` 的 id 关联到对应章节
- `paper_outline.{section}.registry_refs`：该章节会引用的 exp_id 列表
- `writing_order`：先 Experiments、Method，再 Intro/Related Work，最后 Abstract/Conclusion

### Step 5: 写入 + 确认

1. `save_project_file("writing_plan.yaml", yaml_content)` — 写入项目根目录
2. 向 Director 汇报摘要（投稿目标、core claim、章节数、图表数、引用预算）
3. 等待 Director 审批；如有调整，更新 writing_plan.yaml 重新提交

## writing_plan.yaml 格式

```yaml
meta:
  venue: NeurIPS 2026
  track: main
  template: templates/latex/neurips2026/   # Step 3 确认的实际路径
  template_note: ""                         # 复用旧模板时标注原因
  page_limit: 9
  deadline: 2026-06-15
  core_claim: "..."                         # 一句话核心 claim
  created_at: 2026-05-11T14:00:00Z

paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "问题：..."
      - "方法：..."
      - "结果：..."
    dependencies: [experiments, method]

  - section: introduction
    word_budget: 1200
    core_bullets:
      - "Hook: 一个具体、令人惊讶的事实"
      - "Gap: 现有方法的盲点（因为什么导致不够好）"
      - "Insight: 我们发现了什么别人没发现的东西"
      - "Mechanism: 基于 insight 我们做了什么不同的事"
      - "Contributions: [C1, C2, C3]"
    dependencies: [experiments]
    citation_hints:
      - "baseline X 引用原始论文"
      - "dataset Y 引用来源"
    figures: [fig1_overview]

  - section: related_work
    word_budget: 800
    core_bullets:
      - "Cluster 1: ... → 我们的区别"
      - "Cluster 2: ... → 我们的区别"
    dependencies: [introduction]

  - section: method
    word_budget: 1500
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem formulation"
      - "Proposed method"
      - "Theoretical justification"
    dependencies: []
    notation_table:
      X: "input features"
      Y: "target labels"

  - section: experiments
    word_budget: 2000
    core_bullets:
      - "Setup: datasets, baselines, metrics"
      - "Main results: Table 1"
      - "Ablation: Table 2"
      - "Analysis"
    dependencies: []
    registry_refs: [exp_001, exp_002, exp_003]
    tables: [tab1_main_results, tab2_ablation, tab3_hyperparams]
    figures: [fig2_main_results, fig3_ablation]

  - section: conclusion
    word_budget: 400
    core_bullets:
      - "Summary"
      - "Limitations (honest)"
      - "Future work"
    dependencies: [experiments, method]

visualization_plan:
  - fig_id: fig1_overview
    type: conceptual              # conceptual | statistical
    tool: paperbanana             # 概念图走 paperbanana
    description: "系统架构概览图"
    placement: introduction
    aspect_ratio: "16:9"

  - fig_id: fig2_main_results
    type: statistical
    tool: matplotlib              # 统计图走 matplotlib
    description: "主实验结果对比柱状图"
    data_source: "registry: exp_001, exp_002"

  - related_work
  - abstract
  - conclusion
```

## Story Arc（写作前必须回答）

在 `meta.core_claim` 中只写一句话核心 claim，但生成 writing_plan.yaml 前内部必须回答完整 Story Arc，并将关键答案分散到对应章节的 `core_bullets`：

1. **Hook**: 读者为什么应该关心？（具体、令人惊讶的事实/矛盾，不是泛泛"很重要"）→ Introduction 第一条 bullet
2. **Gap**: 现有方法的核心盲点是什么？（不是"不够好"，而是"因为 X 导致不够好"）→ Introduction
3. **Insight**: 我们发现了什么别人没发现的东西？→ 必须能回答；回答不上来说明还没准备好写
4. **Mechanism**: 基于 insight，我们的方法做了什么不同的事？→ Method
5. **Evidence**: 最强的一个数字是什么？→ Abstract / Experiments

## 禁止清单（写入 Worker prompt 时强制下传）

以下句式在全文禁止：
- "XXX has achieved remarkable success in recent years"
- "This demonstrates the effectiveness of our approach"
- "To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to..."
- "Extensive experiments demonstrate that..."

## 约束

- 时间线基于当前日期和 `meta.deadline` 倒推，按 AI 团队速度估 buffer：初稿 1-2 天（Paper Agent 全流水线）、内审 1 天（Reviewer 即时）、修订 1-2 天、提交准备 0.5 天。**不要按人类"初稿 2 周 + 内审 1 周"的节奏留 buffer**
- `paper_outline.{section}.registry_refs` 必须真实存在于 registry，引用未完成实验时在 `core_bullets` 标注 "[TODO exp_xxx]"
- `table_plan.data_source` 写明从 registry 哪些 exp_id 抽数，便于 Worker 后续 `write_paper_section` 时构建 provenance
- 不要过度承诺——只列实际能做完的实验；时间紧张时砍低优先级维度（P2/P3），集中火力在核心 claim，**禁止自行降级目标 venue**（venue 决策是 Director + 用户的权限）
- writing_plan.yaml 是合约——一旦 Director 审批通过，下游 Worker 严格按此执行；如需修改重新提交 Director 审批

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Models.}
8	We evaluate on three architectures spanning different grouped-query attention (GQA) configurations:
9	\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA ratio 7:1, 28 layers $\times$ 4 KV heads = 112 KV heads),
10	\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256 KV heads),
11	and \textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256 KV heads, sliding window attention).
12	This selection covers the two dominant KV head counts (112 vs.\ 256) and both standard and sliding-window attention.
13	
14	\paragraph{Evaluation.}
15	We report perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.
16	For downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.
17	
18	\paragraph{Profiling.}
19	Per-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.
20	Calibration uses 64 sequences of 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train.
21	
22	\paragraph{Compression and constraint.}
23	The default target is 4$\times$ compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio 0.25).
24	The cardinality constraint limits 2-bit assignments to at most $k$ heads, where $k$ is selected via the compounding sweep described in \S\ref{sec:method} ($k{=}8$ for Qwen's 112 heads; analogous sweeps determine $k$ for Llama and Mistral).
25	
26	\paragraph{Baselines.}
27	We compare against:
28	(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;
29	(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\cite{zuo2026ratequant});
30	(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;
31	(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; we report mean$\pm$std and median);
32	and (5)~a naive positional heuristic that assigns Layer-0 to 8-bit and the $k$ deepest heads to 2-bit.
33	
34	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
35	\subsection{Main Results}
36	\label{sec:main_results}
37	
38	\begin{table}[t]
39	\centering
40	\small
41	\caption{PPL ($\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\times$ compression. Unconstrained allocation fails catastrophically on $\{2,4,8,16\}$; our cardinality constraint restores performance. Best constrained result per model in \textbf{bold}.}
42	\label{tab:main_results}
43	\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
44	\toprule
45	Model & Baseline & Uniform & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Unconstrained} & Ours \\
46	 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & Greedy & MCKP & (Constr.) \\
47	\midrule
48	Qwen2.5-7B      & 9.81  & 15.45 & 32.45 & 36.92 & \textbf{10.91} \\
49	Llama-3.1-8B    & 8.09  & 8.47  & ---   & ---   & \textbf{8.45} \\
50	Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.04  & 7.13  & ---   & ---   & 7.16 \\
51	\bottomrule
52	\end{tabular}
53	\end{table}
54	
55	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} summarizes the main results.
56	On Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP achieves 10.91 PPL, a 29.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45).
57	Without the cardinality constraint, both greedy (32.45) and MCKP (36.92) perform \emph{worse} than uniform---a catastrophic failure caused by excessive 2-bit assignments that compound across layers.
58	The constraint eliminates this failure mode entirely.
59	
60	On Llama-3.1-8B, the improvement is marginal: 8.45 vs.\ 8.47 (0.2\%).
61	The profiler finds low sensitivity heterogeneity across Llama's 256 KV heads, leaving little room for non-uniform allocation to improve over uniform.
62	
63	On Mistral-7B-v0.3, constrained MCKP (7.16) is slightly worse than uniform (7.13, $+$0.4\%).
64	This is a genuine negative result: the profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads, meaning the optimization has no reliable signal to exploit.
65	Mistral's sliding-window attention may contribute to this uniformity by limiting head-level variation in effective context length.
66	
67	Unconstrained results for Llama and Mistral are omitted (---) as those experiments were conducted only on Qwen, where the failure mode is most pronounced.
68	Figure~\ref{fig:allocation} visualizes the bit-width allocation on Qwen, showing how constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit while selectively assigning only the 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.
69	
70	\begin{figure}[t]
71	\centering
72	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_allocation_comparison.pdf}
73	\caption{Bit-width allocation on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Uniform assigns all heads to 4-bit. Constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit and assigns the 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.}
74	\label{fig:allocation}
75	\end{figure}
76	
77	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
78	\subsection{Budget Sweep}
79	\label{sec:budget_sweep}
80	
81	\begin{table}[t]
82	\centering
83	\small
84	\caption{Effect of compression ratio on Qwen2.5-7B. Constrained MCKP provides meaningful gains at moderate-to-aggressive compression ($\geq$4$\times$).}
85	\label{tab:budget_sweep}
86	\begin{tabular}{cccc}
87	\toprule
88	Compression & Uniform PPL & Constr.\ MCKP PPL & $\Delta$ PPL \\
89	\midrule
90	2$\times$ & 10.10 & 10.66 & $-$0.56 \\
91	4$\times$ & 15.45 & 11.23 & $+$4.21 \\
92	8$\times$ & 14{,}759 & 907 & $+$13{,}852 \\
93	\bottomrule
94	\end{tabular}
95	\end{table}
96	
97	Table~\ref{tab:budget_sweep} shows how the benefit of constrained allocation varies with compression ratio on Qwen2.5-7B.
98	
99	At 2$\times$ compression, uniform 8-bit quantization is near-lossless (10.10 PPL vs.\ 9.81 bf16, $+$0.29).
100	Per-head optimization has no headroom here; constrained MCKP is slightly worse (10.66) due to unnecessary 2-bit assignments that the budget permits but the model does not need.
101	
102	At 4$\times$, the gap is substantial: constrained MCKP reduces PPL from 15.45 to 11.23, a 27.3\% improvement.
103	This is the regime where non-uniform allocation matters most.
104	
105	At 8$\times$, both methods degrade catastrophically---the budget is too aggressive for any allocation to preserve model quality.
106	However, constrained MCKP (907) is an order of magnitude better than uniform (14{,}759) because the constraint still protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit, preventing total representational collapse.
107	Neither result is practically usable, but the gap demonstrates the protection mechanism at work.
108	
109	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
110	\subsection{Heuristic Baselines}
111	\label{sec:heuristic}
112	
113	\begin{table}[t]
114	\centering
115	\small
116	\caption{Constrained MCKP vs.\ heuristic baselines at 4$\times$ compression. L0-random reports median and mean$\pm$std over 5 seeds.}
117	\label{tab:heuristic}
118	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
119	\toprule
120	Model & MCKP & \multicolumn{2}{c}{L0-random} & Naive \\
121	 & & Median & Mean$\pm$Std & Positional \\
122	\midrule
123	Qwen2.5-7B      & 10.91 & 11.52 & 11.69$\pm$0.42 & 12.23 \\
124	Llama-3.1-8B    & 8.45  & 10.04 & 10.48$\pm$1.03 & --- \\
125	Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.32  & 7.59  & 7.56$\pm$0.09  & --- \\
126	\bottomrule
127	\end{tabular}
128	\end{table}
129	
130	Table~\ref{tab:heuristic} compares profiling-guided MCKP against heuristic baselines that use the same Layer-0 protection but assign 2-bit heads without profiling.
131	
132	On Qwen, MCKP (10.91) beats the L0-random median (11.52) by 0.61 PPL and the naive positional heuristic (12.23) by 1.32 PPL, confirming that profiling-guided selection outperforms both random and depth-based assignment.
133	
134	On Llama, the gap is larger: MCKP achieves 8.45 vs.\ L0-random median 10.04.
135	The high variance of L0-random on this architecture (std$=$1.03) indicates that 2-bit assignment is position-sensitive on 256-head models, making random selection unreliable.
136	
137	On Mistral, the gap is small (7.32 vs.\ 7.59), consistent with the low heterogeneity observed in \S\ref{sec:main_results}.
138	The low L0-random variance (std$=$0.09) further confirms that head sensitivities are nearly uniform, so the choice of which heads receive 2-bit has little impact.
139	
140	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
141	\subsection{Downstream Evaluation}
142	\label{sec:downstream}
143	
144	\begin{table}[t]
145	\centering
146	\small
147	\caption{0-shot accuracy on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Constrained MCKP recovers 72.8\% of the accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit quantization.}
148	\label{tab:downstream}
149	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
150	\toprule
151	Task & Baseline & Uniform & MCKP & $\Delta$ vs \\
152	 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & (Ours) & Uniform \\
153	\midrule
154	ARC-C      & ---   & 0.482 & 0.514 & $+$3.2 pts \\
155	HellaSwag  & ---   & 0.728 & 0.768 & $+$4.0 pts \\
156	PIQA       & ---   & 0.766 & 0.779 & $+$1.3 pts \\
157	WinoGrande & ---   & 0.662 & 0.682 & $+$2.0 pts \\
158	\midrule
159	Average    & 0.695 & 0.660 & 0.686 & $+$2.6 pts \\
160	\bottomrule
161	\end{tabular}
162	\end{table}
163	
164	Table~\ref{tab:downstream} shows that the PPL improvements transfer to downstream tasks on Qwen2.5-7B.
165	Constrained MCKP improves average 0-shot accuracy by 2.6 points over uniform 4-bit (0.686 vs.\ 0.660), with gains on all four benchmarks.
166	The largest gain appears on HellaSwag ($+$4.0 pts), where language modeling quality is most directly reflected.
167	
168	The recovery rate---the fraction of accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit that constrained MCKP recovers---is $(0.686 - 0.660) / (0.695 - 0.660) = 72.8\%$.
169	This indicates that per-head bit allocation addresses much of the degradation introduced by uniform quantization, though a gap to bf16 remains.
170

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Models.}
8	We evaluate on three architectures spanning different grouped-query attention (GQA) configurations:
9	\textbf{Qwen2.5-7B} (GQA ratio 7:1, 28 layers $\times$ 4 KV heads = 112 KV heads),
10	\textbf{Llama-3.1-8B} (4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256 KV heads),
11	and \textbf{Mistral-7B-v0.3} (4:1, 32 $\times$ 8 = 256 KV heads, sliding window attention).
12	This selection covers the two dominant KV head counts (112 vs.\ 256) and both standard and sliding-window attention.
13	
14	\paragraph{Evaluation.}
15	We report perplexity (PPL, $\downarrow$) on the WikiText-2 test split (298{,}938 tokens) under bf16 inference with stride 512.
16	For downstream evaluation, we use ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, and WinoGrande under 0-shot prompting.
17	
18	\paragraph{Profiling.}
19	Per-head sensitivity is measured by independently quantizing each head to each candidate bit-width in $\{2, 4, 8, 16\}$ and recording the PPL increase over the bf16 baseline.
20	Calibration uses 64 sequences of 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train.
21	
22	\paragraph{Compression and constraint.}
23	The default target is 4$\times$ compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio 0.25).
24	The cardinality constraint limits 2-bit assignments to at most $k$ heads, where $k$ is selected via the compounding sweep described in \S\ref{sec:method} ($k{=}8$ for Qwen's 112 heads; analogous sweeps determine $k$ for Llama and Mistral).
25	
26	\paragraph{Baselines.}
27	We compare against:
28	(1)~uniform 4-bit quantization;
29	(2)~unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style~\cite{zuo2026ratequant});
30	(3)~unconstrained MCKP allocation;
31	(4)~an L0-random heuristic that assigns Layer-0 heads to 8-bit and $k$ random non-Layer-0 heads to 2-bit, with remaining heads at 4-bit (5 seeds; we report mean$\pm$std and median);
32	and (5)~a naive positional heuristic that assigns Layer-0 to 8-bit and the $k$ deepest heads to 2-bit.
33	
34	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
35	\subsection{Main Results}
36	\label{sec:main_results}
37	
38	\begin{table}[t]
39	\centering
40	\small
41	\caption{PPL ($\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\times$ compression. Unconstrained allocation fails catastrophically on $\{2,4,8,16\}$; our cardinality constraint restores performance. Best constrained result per model in \textbf{bold}.}
42	\label{tab:main_results}
43	\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
44	\toprule
45	Model & Baseline & Uniform & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Unconstrained} & Ours \\
46	 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & Greedy & MCKP & (Constr.) \\
47	\midrule
48	Qwen2.5-7B      & 9.81  & 15.45 & 32.45 & 36.92 & \textbf{10.91} \\
49	Llama-3.1-8B    & 8.09  & 8.47  & ---   & ---   & \textbf{8.45} \\
50	Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.04  & 7.13  & ---   & ---   & 7.16 \\
51	\bottomrule
52	\end{tabular}
53	\end{table}
54	
55	Table~\ref{tab:main_results} summarizes the main results.
56	On Qwen2.5-7B, constrained MCKP achieves 10.91 PPL, a 29.3\% reduction over uniform 4-bit (15.45).
57	Without the cardinality constraint, both greedy (32.45) and MCKP (36.92) perform \emph{worse} than uniform---a catastrophic failure caused by excessive 2-bit assignments that compound across layers.
58	The constraint eliminates this failure mode entirely.
59	
60	On Llama-3.1-8B, the improvement is marginal: 8.45 vs.\ 8.47 (0.2\%).
61	The profiler finds low sensitivity heterogeneity across Llama's 256 KV heads, leaving little room for non-uniform allocation to improve over uniform.
62	
63	On Mistral-7B-v0.3, constrained MCKP (7.16) is slightly worse than uniform (7.13, $+$0.4\%).
64	This is a genuine negative result: the profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads, meaning the optimization has no reliable signal to exploit.
65	Mistral's sliding-window attention may contribute to this uniformity by limiting head-level variation in effective context length.
66	
67	Unconstrained results for Llama and Mistral are omitted (---) as those experiments were conducted only on Qwen, where the failure mode is most pronounced.
68	Figure~\ref{fig:allocation} visualizes the bit-width allocation on Qwen, showing how constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit while selectively assigning only the 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.
69	
70	\begin{figure}[t]
71	\centering
72	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_allocation_comparison.pdf}
73	\caption{Bit-width allocation on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Uniform assigns all heads to 4-bit. Constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit and assigns the 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.}
74	\label{fig:allocation}
75	\end{figure}
76	
77	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
78	\subsection{Budget Sweep}
79	\label{sec:budget_sweep}
80	
81	\begin{table}[t]
82	\centering
83	\small
84	\caption{Effect of compression ratio on Qwen2.5-7B (standard-resolution profiling). Constrained MCKP provides meaningful gains at moderate-to-aggressive compression ($\geq$4$\times$). The 4$\times$ MCKP result is slightly higher than Table~\ref{tab:main_results} due to lower profiling resolution; the trend across compression ratios is the primary takeaway.}
85	\label{tab:budget_sweep}
86	\begin{tabular}{cccc}
87	\toprule
88	Compression & Uniform PPL & Constr.\ MCKP PPL & $\Delta$ PPL \\
89	\midrule
90	2$\times$ & 10.10 & 10.66 & $-$0.56 \\
91	4$\times$ & 15.45 & 11.23 & $+$4.21 \\
92	8$\times$ & 14{,}759 & 907 & $+$13{,}852 \\
93	\bottomrule
94	\end{tabular}
95	\end{table}
96	
97	Table~\ref{tab:budget_sweep} shows how the benefit of constrained allocation varies with compression ratio on Qwen2.5-7B.
98	
99	At 2$\times$ compression, uniform 8-bit quantization is near-lossless (10.10 PPL vs.\ 9.81 bf16, $+$0.29).
100	Per-head optimization has no headroom here; constrained MCKP is slightly worse (10.66) due to unnecessary 2-bit assignments that the budget permits but the model does not need.
101	
102	At 4$\times$, the gap is substantial: constrained MCKP reduces PPL from 15.45 to 11.23, a 27.3\% improvement.
103	With hires profiling (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}), this improves further to 10.91 (29.3\%).
104	
105	At 8$\times$, both methods degrade catastrophically---the budget is too aggressive for any allocation to preserve model quality.
106	However, constrained MCKP (907) is an order of magnitude better than uniform (14{,}759) because the constraint still protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit, preventing total representational collapse.
107	Neither result is practically usable, but the gap demonstrates the protection mechanism at work.
108	
109	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
110	\subsection{Heuristic Baselines}
111	\label{sec:heuristic}
112	
113	\begin{table}[t]
114	\centering
115	\small
116	\caption{Constrained MCKP vs.\ heuristic baselines at 4$\times$ compression. L0-random reports median and mean$\pm$std over 5 seeds. All methods use the same $k$ per model ($k{=}8$ for Qwen, $k{=}16$ for Llama/Mistral).}
117	\label{tab:heuristic}
118	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
119	\toprule
120	Model & MCKP & \multicolumn{2}{c}{L0-random} & Naive \\
121	 & & Median & Mean$\pm$Std & Positional \\
122	\midrule
123	Qwen2.5-7B      & 10.91 & 11.52 & 11.69$\pm$0.47 & 12.23 \\
124	Llama-3.1-8B    & 8.45  & 10.04 & 10.48$\pm$1.03 & 9.94 \\
125	Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.32  & 7.59  & 7.56$\pm$0.09  & 7.48 \\
126	\bottomrule
127	\end{tabular}
128	\end{table}
129	
130	Table~\ref{tab:heuristic} compares profiling-guided MCKP against heuristic baselines that use the same Layer-0 protection but assign 2-bit heads without profiling.
131	
132	On Qwen, MCKP (10.91) beats the L0-random median (11.52) by 0.61 PPL and the naive positional heuristic (12.23) by 1.32 PPL, confirming that profiling-guided selection outperforms both random and depth-based assignment.
133	
134	On Llama, the gap is larger: MCKP achieves 8.45 vs.\ L0-random median 10.04.
135	The high variance of L0-random on this architecture (std$=$1.03) indicates that 2-bit assignment is position-sensitive on 256-head models, making random selection unreliable.
136	The naive positional heuristic (9.94) performs better than random but still 1.49 PPL worse than MCKP, confirming that depth alone is an imperfect proxy for head sensitivity.
137	
138	On Mistral, the gap is small (7.32 vs.\ 7.59), consistent with the low heterogeneity observed in \S\ref{sec:main_results}.
139	The low L0-random variance (std$=$0.09) further confirms that head sensitivities are nearly uniform, so the choice of which heads receive 2-bit has little impact.
140	All non-uniform strategies (MCKP 7.32, naive 7.48, L0-random 7.56) are worse than uniform 4-bit (7.13) on this architecture, reinforcing that non-uniform allocation is counterproductive when heterogeneity is low.
141	
142	% ------------------------------------------------------------------
143	\subsection{Downstream Evaluation}
144	\label{sec:downstream}
145	
146	\begin{table}[t]
147	\centering
148	\small
149	\caption{0-shot accuracy on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Constrained MCKP recovers 72.8\% of the accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit quantization.}
150	\label{tab:downstream}
151	\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
152	\toprule
153	Task & Baseline & Uniform & MCKP & $\Delta$ vs \\
154	 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & (Ours) & Uniform \\
155	\midrule
156	ARC-C      & ---   & 0.482 & 0.514 & $+$3.2 pts \\
157	HellaSwag  & ---   & 0.728 & 0.768 & $+$4.0 pts \\
158	PIQA       & ---   & 0.766 & 0.779 & $+$1.3 pts \\
159	WinoGrande & ---   & 0.662 & 0.682 & $+$2.0 pts \\
160	\midrule
161	Average    & 0.695 & 0.660 & 0.686 & $+$2.6 pts \\
162	\bottomrule
163	\end{tabular}
164	\end{table}
165	
166	Table~\ref{tab:downstream} shows that the PPL improvements transfer to downstream tasks on Qwen2.5-7B.
167	Constrained MCKP improves average 0-shot accuracy by 2.6 points over uniform 4-bit (0.686 vs.\ 0.660), with gains on all four benchmarks.
168	The largest gain appears on HellaSwag ($+$4.0 pts), where language modeling quality is most directly reflected.
169	
170	The recovery rate---the fraction of accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit that constrained MCKP recovers---is 72.8\%, indicating that per-head bit allocation addresses much of the degradation introduced by uniform quantization, though a gap to bf16 remains.

# ── Story Arc (internal, distilled into section bullets) ──
# Hook: Both greedy and MCKP produce catastrophic PPL (32–37) on {2,4,8,16} despite working on consecutive integers
# Gap: (1) Polymatroid structure breaks on non-consecutive bit-widths → additive distortion assumption fails;
#      (2) No framework for deciding WHEN non-uniform KV cache quantization helps
# Insight: Root cause is 2-bit compounding — profiler distortions are non-additive; a cardinality cap is the minimal fix
# Mechanism: (a) cap 2-bit assignments → prevents compounding → solver choice irrelevant; (b) heterogeneity predicts benefit
# Evidence: Qwen 10.91 vs 15.45 (−29.3%); solver Δ=0.0000 across 3 models

paper_outline:
  - section: abstract
    word_budget: 200
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem: per-head mixed-precision KV cache quantization on hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16} fails — both greedy (PPL 32) and MCKP (PPL 37) collapse"
      - "Root cause: 2-bit compounding — per-head distortions non-additive when many heads at extreme quantization"
      - "Fix: cardinality constraint (max_2bit≤k); solver-agnostic (greedy = MCKP, Δ=0.0000)"
      - "Result: 29.3% PPL improvement on high-heterogeneity architecture (Qwen, 10.91 vs 15.45)"
      - "Analysis: head sensitivity concentration diagnostic — Top-5% > 0.50 → non-uniform; profiling distortion ≈ 0 → uniform"
    dependencies: [experiments, method, analysis]

  - section: introduction
    word_budget: 900
    core_bullets:
      - "Hook: Per-head KV cache quantization should reduce memory while preserving quality. Yet on hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16} bit-widths, both greedy and MCKP — the two dominant allocation algorithms — produce catastrophic PPL 32–37, far worse than uniform 4-bit (15.45)."
      - "Gap: (1) RateQuant's greedy is provably optimal on consecutive integers {2,...,6} (Prop. 6) but polymatroid structure breaks on non-consecutive {2,4,8,16}; (2) MCKP also fails due to non-additive distortion compounding; (3) No existing work addresses WHEN non-uniform allocation is beneficial."
      - "Insight: The root cause is 2-bit compounding — unconstrained solvers assign 68–75 heads to 2-bit, where per-head distortions compound non-additively. A cardinality cap on 2-bit assignments is the minimal sufficient intervention."
      - "Mechanism: (a) cardinality constraint max_2bit≤k; (b) constraint alone makes solver choice irrelevant — constrained greedy = constrained MCKP (Δ=0.0000); (c) benefit depends on head sensitivity heterogeneity."
      - "Contributions: [C1] Identify compounding failure + cardinality fix for hardware-aligned bit-widths; [C2] Prove solver equivalence under constraint (greedy=MCKP, 3-model per-head verification); [C3] Heterogeneity-based diagnostic framework for when non-uniform allocation is worthwhile."

  - section: related_work

      - "Mixed-precision rate-distortion allocation (RateQuant, ARKV, SqueezeLLM): RateQuant optimal on consecutive integers but fails on {2,4,8,16}; we provide the fix (constraint) + the missing 'when to use' analysis"
      - "Attention head analysis (Voita et al. 2019, Michel et al. 2019): head importance/pruning → we study quantization sensitivity heterogeneity as a distinct phenomenon"
    dependencies: [introduction]

  - section: method
    word_budget: 900
    core_bullets:
      - "§3.1 Problem formulation: per-head bit-width allocation as constrained optimization. Action space B={2,4,8,16}. Memory budget constraint. Objective: minimize total PPL degradation."
      - "§3.2 PPL-based per-head profiling: quantize each head independently, measure PPL increase d_h(b). Additive distortion assumption: total ≈ Σ d_h(b_h)."
      - "§3.3 Compounding effect: why additivity fails. When many heads at 2-bit simultaneously, actual PPL >> Σ individual d_h(2). Empirical: unconstrained assigns 68–75 heads to 2-bit → PPL 32–37 vs predicted ~11."

      - "§3.5 Solver equivalence: constrained greedy = constrained MCKP (Δ=0.0000). Constraint narrows feasible set so greedy's local decisions are globally optimal. Per-head verification: Qwen 112/112, Llama 256/256, Mistral 255/256 (1 zero-distortion tie)."

      B: "feasible bit-width set {2,4,8,16}"
      d_h(b): "profiled distortion (PPL increase) when head h quantized to b bits"
      R: "memory budget ratio (e.g. 0.25 for 4× compression)"
